descSections.overview:
Blue/Yellow value-midrange: cheap Programs and Gears draw cards and shape Gig values while Blockers hold the line.
Wins by landing 8-10 power Units (@[Rockn' Rockerboy], @[Jackie Welles: Ride or Die Choom], @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel]) that steal Gigs.
descSections.early:
Turn 1-2: cheap plays like @[Floor It], @[Trust No One], @[Mandibular Upgrade] or @[Zetatech Faceplate] to start drawing and make a min Gig.
Land @[Rita Wheeler: No Stupid Questions] on turn 2-3 to loot and block, or @[Mox Inciters] to force a rival Unit to attack into your board.
Goal: smooth hand and keep Gigs safe, not race.
descSections.mid:
Add @[Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon] to replay a Program from trash for free, and @[Rockn' Rockerboy] at 5 for the first real threat.
Use @[Bootleg Black Sapphire Show] when you hold both an even and an odd Gig, for Eddies plus 2 cards.
Equip Gears on Blockers so they draw and block at once.
descSections.late:
Drop @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel], discarding a spare Program to bottom-deck the rival's best Unit, then attack to steal 2.
@[Jackie Welles: Ride or Die Choom] gets huge with even Gigs, so tune Gig values with @[Zetatech Faceplate] before swinging.
Swing at spent rival Units or the Gig area, keeping a Blocker back.
descSections.combos:
@[Trust No One] - creates min Gigs; feeds @[Jackie Welles: Pour One Out For Me], draws itself, and is the best Program to replay with Lizzy.
@[Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon] - turns cheap Programs from trash into repeated value and @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel|Placide] fodder.
@[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] - the only repeatable removal and a 2-steal finisher; needs Programs to discard.
@[Rita Wheeler: No Stupid Questions] - loots and protects, converting spare cards into Program fodder.
@[Zetatech Faceplate] - draw engine on every spend and tunes Gig parity for Ride or Die Choom and Bootleg.
descSections.mulligan: Keep hands with 2+ cheap plays (@[Floor It], @[Trust No One], Gear) plus a Blocker like @[Rita Wheeler: No Stupid Questions]. Sellable cards are fine fodder for Eddies, so a hand with one big Unit and cheap setup is acceptable. Bad alone: @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel], @[Jackie Welles: Ride or Die Choom], @[Bootleg Black Sapphire Show], and @[Live with the Aftermath] without a Unit. Mulligan hands with only expensive cards or only Gears and no Units.
descSections.mulliganFirst: Going first, Eddies are scarce, so want 1-cost plays on turn 1 (@[Floor It], @[Trust No One], @[Mandibular Upgrade]) and a 3-4 cost Unit for turn 2. Turn 1 is cheap setup; turn 2 lands @[Rita Wheeler: No Stupid Questions] or @[Mox Inciters]. Sell spare cards to reach the 5-cost Units.
descSections.mulliganSecond:
Going second, with all Legends ready, a 3-4 cost Unit on turn 1 is possible, so keep Blockers plus cheap draw.
You can see the rival's board, so keep @[Mox Inciters] or @[Floor It] against an aggressive start.
A hand with @[Rockn' Rockerboy] plus cheap setup is fine, since turn 2-3 reaches 5.
descSections.notes:
Lowering your own Gigs with @[Trust No One] and @[Jackie Welles: Pour One Out For Me] can lose Street Cred and fights for Gigs; don't over-use it.
The deck has only 7 finishers and little removal, so a fast aggro start can steal Gigs before the big Units arrive.
Dead or weak draws like @[Adrenaline Converter] and @[Viktor Vektor: Drop Your Illusions] can be sold or ignored.

descSections.overview:
Blue Green Program-control deck that draws through cheap Programs and bottom-decks every rival Unit.
It wins by stealing Gigs through the cleared board, with @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] as the main closer.
descSections.early: Turns 1-2: cheap Programs like @[Trust No One], @[Floor It] and @[Peace Offering] to smooth draws; a @[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy] as the first body. Use @[Trust No One] to push a Gig down toward a min Gig, which switches on @[Three Mouths, One Desire] and @[Chrome Reverie]. Sell spare Programs if Eddies are short; keep removal for real threats.
descSections.mid:
Turn 3-4: @[Delamain: Rideshare AI] or @[Three Mouths, One Desire] to refill, then @[Pyramid Song] or @[Les Élémens] on the first real rival Unit.
@[Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon] gives a Blocker and replays a cheap Program from the trash for free.
@[Maman Brigitte: Spirit of Death] turns two surplus Programs into a bottom-decked rival Unit.
descSections.late:
Land @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] and discard a Program on play, then on each attack, to keep clearing blockers.
Use @[Chrome Reverie] and @[Nocturne OP55 N1] to stop the last rival attackers while Voodoo Boys, Brigitte and @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel|Placide] steal the Gigs.
Use @[Judy Álvarez: Braindance Maestro] and @[Delamain: Rideshare AI|Delamain] to keep Programs coming.
descSections.combos:
@[Trust No One] - lowers Gigs to min and draws; feeds @[Three Mouths, One Desire], @[Chrome Reverie], @[Pyramid Song] and Jackie.
@[Maman Brigitte: Spirit of Death] - converts excess Programs into removal; the deck depends on it as a repeatable cost sink.
@[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] - the finisher: removal each attack and a 2-Gig steal.
@[Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon] - replays Programs from the trash, a free @[Pyramid Song] or @[Trust No One].
@[Les Élémens] - clean unconditional removal when fights are unfavorable.
descSections.mulligan:
Keep hands with 2-3 cheap Programs plus a Unit or a draw piece like @[Delamain: Rideshare AI].
Keep removal (@[Pyramid Song]) only with cheap plays to reach it.
@[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] and @[Les Élémens] are dead early, so a hand with several of them and little else should be redone.
@[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy] is weak without Programs.
descSections.mulliganFirst:
Few Eddies on turns 1-2, so want 1-cost Programs (@[Trust No One], @[Floor It], @[Peace Offering]) and @[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy].
Use the cheap turns to dig and set up a min Gig, ready for turn 3 @[Delamain: Rideshare AI] or @[Three Mouths, One Desire].
Hands with only 5-cost cards are too slow.
descSections.mulliganSecond:
All Legends available so turn 2-3 plays like @[Delamain: Rideshare AI] and @[Pyramid Song] are easier.
Look at the rival's board: keep removal like @[Pyramid Song] against early Units, and @[Les Élémens] if a slow hand has plenty of draw.
Aim for a hand that casts a Program each turn.
descSections.notes:
Fast aggro steals Gigs before the engine works, and the deck's power is low in fights.
Discarding Programs to Brigitte/@[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel|Placide] with weak draws can run out of gas; watch the deck count with heavy draw.
The Green splash (@[Peace Offering], @[Memory Relapse]) is small and Hanako needs value-pairs, so it is a minor synergy.

descSections.overview:
Blue-Green Program control deck that chains cheap Gig-lowering and draw Programs, bottom-decks every rival Unit, and gets value from min Gigs.
It wins by attacking an emptied board with Units like @[MaxTac AV] and @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] to steal the Gigs it needs.
descSections.early: Turns 1-2: play 1-cost Programs (@[Trust No One], @[Floor It], @[Peace Offering]) to dig, create a min Gig and keep a Program in hand or trash for later. Add @[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy] or @[NetWatch Netdriver] when mana is spare. Sell extra copies of expensive Programs if Eddies are short. Goal: have a min Gig online and Programs in the trash before turn 3.
descSections.mid:
Use @[Three Mouths, One Desire] with a min Gig to take extra cards, and @[Chrome Reverie] to stall a rival attacker and Call a Legend for free.
Land @[Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon] to replay a cheap Program from trash for free, ideally @[Pyramid Song] or @[Trust No One].
Answer rival Units with @[Pyramid Song] and @[Les Élémens]; use @[Maman Brigitte: Spirit of Death] when you have spare Programs to discard.
descSections.late:
Reach @[MaxTac AV], @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles] and @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] to attack once the rival board is clear.
@[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] discards a Program to remove a Unit each attack and steals 2 Gigs at 10 power.
Keep @[Take Control] and @[Floor It] up to protect Gigs during the rival's attacks.
descSections.combos:
@[Trust No One] - cheap way to make a min Gig and draw; it turns on @[Three Mouths, One Desire], @[Chrome Reverie], @[Pyramid Song] and @[Alt Cunningham: Soulkiller Architect|Alt Cunningham].
@[Three Mouths, One Desire] - search that scales with min Gigs and keeps the Program chain going.
@[Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon] - replays a cheap Program from trash and provides a Blocker for the setup turns.
@[Pyramid Song] - the key removal; both modes are available with a d4 at min.
@[Alt Cunningham: Soulkiller Architect] - discounts Programs with min Gigs and replays them from trash.
descSections.mulligan: Keep hands with 2-3 cheap Programs (@[Trust No One], @[Floor It], @[Peace Offering], @[Three Mouths, One Desire]) plus a Unit to play. A hand of only @[Les Élémens] or @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] with no cheap plays is a mulligan. @[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy] alone does nothing without Programs. Sellable extras help hit Eddies.
descSections.mulliganFirst:
With few Eddies at the start, want 1-cost Programs and a 2-3 cost play. Use turns 1-2 to make a min Gig and draw.
A hand with @[Trust No One] and @[Three Mouths, One Desire] is great. @[Les Élémens] can be kept only if the rest of the hand is cheap, and later sold or played.
descSections.mulliganSecond:
With all Legends available, you can keep slightly more expensive hands such as @[Chrome Reverie] or @[Pyramid Song], and answer the rival's first Unit.
Look at the rival's board: keep removal if they are aggressive, draw engines if they are slow.
descSections.notes:
Slow starts against aggro lose Gigs before the engine runs.
Too many Programs and too few threatening Units can stall the game into overtime.
Lowering own Gigs to min does little for Street Cred, and the deck depends on stealing.

Few Units and one finisher make the game slow; if your Gigs are stolen first you lose the race.
Discarding Programs to @[Maman Brigitte: Spirit of Death] and @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] can strip the hand.
Wide rival boards beat single-target removal unless @[Towerfall] is available.
Missing 1 @[Towerfall] card
descSections.overview:
Blue Program-control deck that makes min Gigs with cheap Programs, then bottom-decks rival Units with @[Les Élémens], @[Pyramid Song], @[Towerfall] and Unit triggers.
It wins by attacking the cleared board with @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles], @[Psycho Squad] and @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] to steal Gigs up to 7.
descSections.early: Turns 1-2: play @[Trust No One] on a Gig (a d4 first is ideal, so @[Pyramid Song] gets both modes later) and @[Floor It] or @[Peace Offering] to keep drawing. The goal is a min Gig, a full hand and no rival Unit hitting your Gigs.
descSections.mid:
Turns 3-5: @[Three Mouths, One Desire] with min Gigs digs two or three cards deep, and @[Chrome Reverie] freezes an attacker and flips a Legend for free.
Use @[Alt Cunningham: Soulkiller Architect] to discount or replay @[Les Élémens] and @[Pyramid Song].
Land @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles] or @[Psycho Squad] and @[Maman Brigitte: Spirit of Death] or @[Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon] to start trading Programs for rival Units.
descSections.late:
@[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] comes down to remove a Unit on play and again on every attack while stealing 2 Gigs.
@[Towerfall] clears the board, and doubles up when your Street Cred is low from min Gigs.
@[Nocturne OP55 N1] becomes cheap once the fixer area is empty: draw 2 or freeze a Unit for the final attacks.
descSections.combos:
@[Trust No One] - the min-Gig enabler: it also draws, and it turns on @[Three Mouths, One Desire], @[Chrome Reverie], @[Pyramid Song]'s double mode and @[Alt Cunningham: Soulkiller Architect]'s discount.
@[Les Élémens] - the main clean answer; with 3 copies and @[Alt Cunningham: Soulkiller Architect] or @[Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon] it can be reused.
@[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] - the finisher: repeatable removal plus a 2-Gig steal, and it needs the Program count to pay for its discards.
@[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles] - the main 6-power attacker that takes Gigs once the way is clear.
@[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy] - cheap body that attacks once a Program is played, which this deck does every turn.
Best pair: @[Trust No One] into @[Three Mouths, One Desire] the same turn for a bigger dig.
descSections.mulligan:
Keep hands with 2-3 cheap Programs (@[Trust No One], @[Floor It], @[Peace Offering]) plus one Unit or a removal Program.
@[Trust No One] and @[Three Mouths, One Desire] are the best starts since they set up the min-Gig engine.
Expensive @[Les Élémens], @[Towerfall] and @[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel] alone are dead early; Units can't be sold, so avoid hands of only Units.
Mulligan a hand with no 1-2 cost plays.
descSections.mulliganFirst: Going first you have few Eddies, so you want 1-cost Programs for turns 1-2: @[Trust No One] and @[Floor It] to draw and set a min Gig. A hand with only 5+ cost cards is a mulligan.
descSections.mulliganSecond:
Going second you see the rival's board and have all three Legends: turn 1 can be @[Mox Inciters], @[Three Mouths, One Desire] plus a 1-drop, or @[Chrome Reverie].
Keep a hand with removal that answers their first Unit (@[Pyramid Song], @[Floor It]) and some cheap setup.
You can keep a slightly slower hand with one 5-cost card if the early plays are in place.

descSections.overview:
Red midrange-aggro built on 9-10 power bodies backed by a full suite of removal Programs.
It wins by stealing Gigs two at a time with @[Animals Wrecker] and @[Yorinobu Arasaka: Steel Dragon] once the blockers are cleared.
descSections.early: Turns 1-2: @[Mantis Blades], @[Satori: Sword of Saburo] and @[Industrial Assembly] are cheap plays that start Gig tuning. Sell spare Gear and Programs for Eddies to reach the big turns. Turn 3-4: @[Augmented Negotiators] holds the Gig area and @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo] is the first real body. @[Bonnie and Clyde] clears small blockers. The goal is to hit 6-7 Eddies on time, not to race.
descSections.mid:
Turn 5-6: @[Animals Wrecker] is the first steal threat. @[Offduty Malfini] or @[Bonnie and Clyde] open the way for an attack.
Equip Gear to the attacker. @[Satori: Sword of Saburo] draws when it wins a fight, and @[Zetatech Faceplate] draws and nudges a Gig each time the equipped Unit is spent.
Use @[Industrial Assembly], @[Dexter DeShawn: Off the Grid] and @[Muamar Reyes: El Capitán] to push Gigs to 8+. That makes @[Carnage at the Colosseum] cheap and @[Over the Edge] live.
descSections.late:
Turn 7+: @[Yorinobu Arasaka: Steel Dragon] puts @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo] or @[Offduty Malfini] into play for free, even from the trash, and that Unit can attack rival Units right away.
Chain removal into repeated 2-Gig steals until the Gig count reaches 7. @[V: Streetkid] Go Solo adds a 5-cost attacker when Eddies are spare.
@[Dexter DeShawn: Off the Grid] Call gives +2 power to push an attacker over the 10 threshold.
descSections.combos:
@[Yorinobu Arasaka: Steel Dragon] - the top-end engine: it cheats a cheap Unit in from hand or trash and draws when a Unit is lost. @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo] and @[Offduty Malfini] are the best targets.
@[Animals Wrecker] - the main finisher: 10 power steals 2 Gigs per hit and nothing else in the deck does that as cleanly.
@[Offduty Malfini] - spends a rival Unit so your big Unit has a target, and it is a good free target for Yorinobu.
@[Industrial Assembly] - cheap Gig tuning that turns on @[Carnage at the Colosseum] and @[Over the Edge], and draws once a Gig is 8+.
@[Bonnie and Clyde] - cheap removal that clears blockers early and gets better when you are behind on Gigs.
Best pair: @[Offduty Malfini] plus @[Animals Wrecker], or @[Yorinobu Arasaka: Steel Dragon] plus @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo] from the trash.
descSections.mulligan: Keep hands with 2-3 cheap plays (Gear, @[Industrial Assembly], @[Bonnie and Clyde]) plus one Unit of cost 4 or less. Sellable cards matter, because they become the Eddies that pay for the 6-7 drops. A hand of only @[Animals Wrecker], @[Yorinobu Arasaka: Steel Dragon] and other Units cannot be sold and does nothing early. Mulligan it. @[Detonate] and @[Over the Edge] are poor on their own early. They are mostly sell fodder or late-game answers.
descSections.mulliganFirst: With two Legends spent on turn 1, you want cheap plays like @[Mantis Blades], @[Satori: Sword of Saburo] and @[Industrial Assembly] that set up turn 2. Keep one @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo], @[Augmented Negotiators] or @[Bonnie and Clyde] as the turn 3-4 anchor. Sell the spare Gear to build Eddies for the 6-7 drops. Do not keep a hand of two or more expensive Units with no cheap plays.
descSections.mulliganSecond: You have all three Legends ready and can see the rival's opening board. Keep removal like @[Bonnie and Clyde] if their early Units are small. You can afford a hand with one @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo] or @[Offduty Malfini] plus Gear and Programs, and reach @[Animals Wrecker] a turn earlier than going first. Accept a slower hand if it has enough sellable cards to reach 6-7 Eddies.
descSections.notes: Unsellable Units and a 6-7 cost top end make the deck clunky if the hand is Unit-heavy or the Eddies stall. Your attackers stay spent after attacking and can be attacked back. Protect them with @[Muamar Reyes: El Capitán] Call, @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo] and @[Augmented Negotiators] blocking. The deck is thin and draws a lot, and @[V: Streetkid] Call trashes 3, so watch the deck size in long games.

descSections.overview:
Gear-equipped midrange: put cheap Gears on sturdy Units to win fights and steal Gigs, drawing extra cards off Gear and Gig triggers.
Wins by stealing the Gigs needed for 7, with @[Gorilla Arms] double steals and @[Jackie Welles: Ride or Die Choom] as the biggest attackers.
descSections.early:
Play a Unit on turn 1-2, with @[Secondhand Bombus] or @[Swordwise Huscle] as the cheap options, and hold Gears for the next turn.
Use @[Mantis Blades] and @[Zetatech Faceplate] as cheap equips; @[River Ward: Detective on the Hunt] makes them free.
Get a Gig-adjusting Gear online early to set up even/odd values.
descSections.mid:
Land @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo] or @[6th Street Recruits], equip, and attack spent rival Units to trade up and draw off @[Satori: Sword of Saburo].
Add @[Gorilla Arms] to a Unit that can connect to the Gig area.
Cast @[Bootleg Black Sapphire Show] once you have even and odd Gigs for a refill.
descSections.late:
Play @[Jackie Welles: Ride or Die Choom] or @[Johnny Silverhand: Never Stop Fighting] with Gears for double steals and repeat attacks.
Use @[Over the Edge] or @[Live with the Aftermath] to clear the one blocker standing in the way.
Keep a Blocker back to protect your Gigs while you close out the last steals.
descSections.combos:
@[Gorilla Arms] - the finisher Gear; doubles steals and shortens the clock to 7 Gigs.
@[River Ward: Detective on the Hunt] - turns 1-2 cost Gears into free plays at Quick speed and digs when equipped Units die.
@[Zetatech Faceplate] - adjusts Gigs and draws; powers the even/odd payoffs.
@[Jackie Welles: Ride or Die Choom] - the top-end threat that needs mixed Gig values and rewards the adjusting plan.
@[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo] - sturdy Blocker/attacker that carries Gears while protecting the Gig area.
descSections.mulligan:
Keep hands with a Unit plus two or more cheap Gears or draw sources.
A Unit that can carry Gears (@[Swordwise Huscle], @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo]) is the anchor.
Gears alone are dead; @[Bootleg Black Sapphire Show], @[Jackie Welles: Ride or Die Choom] and @[Gorilla Arms] are bad early without a setup.
descSections.mulliganFirst:
Going first, you have only one Legend to pay with on turn 1, so you want cheap plays. A 2-cost Unit like @[Secondhand Bombus] and a Gear like @[Mantis Blades] to follow is ideal.
Use the first turns to put Units out, because Gears equip later with more Eddies.
Expensive cards are fine only if a cheap Unit and a Gear are also in hand.
descSections.mulliganSecond:
Going second, all Legends are ready, so a 4-cost Unit like @[6th Street Recruits] or @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo] on turn 1-2 is viable.
You can see the rival's board; keep removal or a Blocker if they are aggressive.
Keep hands with a Unit plus a Gear and a Legend Call to build momentum.
descSections.notes:
The deck loses if its Units are removed or traded off and the Gears are stranded.
Against fast aggro with many Gigs it can fall behind on Gig count; @[Adrenaline Converter] is the comeback tool.
The 0-power @[Secondhand Bombus] and the unreliable @[Over the Edge] limit proactive plays.

Missing Johnny

descSections.overview: Win the Gig (dice) battle and out-draw your opponent. Push your Gigs down to min with @[Trust No One] and @[Peace Offering] to draw cards, steal Gigs, and remove key units. Value pairs of Gigs let @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles|Pepe] ready your Merc Legends and power Hanako’s draw. Your three Legends are Jackie, Alt and Hanako.
descSections.early:
Going first - Turn 1: @[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy|Voodoo Boy], or @[Trust No One] plus calling a Legend.
Going second - you start with 4 resources and all Legends ready. Turn-1 @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles|Pepe] is strong against most decks. Against blue/green, keep a hand that answers @[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy|Voodoo Boy].
descSections.mid: Turn 2: @[Les Élémens], @[Pyramid Song], or @[Chrome Reverie]. Roll Gigs from the smallest die (D4) upward. Play @[Nocturne OP55 N1|Nocturne] early so Alt or Lizzy can reuse it.
descSections.late: Aim for turns with a double @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles|Pepe], using value pairs of Gigs to ready your Merc Legends. @[Towerfall] is the sweeper (-5 to all rival units). Keep key Programs in your trash for Alt, especially @[Les Élémens].
descSections.combos:
@[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy] (2 cost, 2 power): can’t attack unless you played a Program that turn. It’s the best turn-1 play going first.
@[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles|Pepe Najarro] (4 cost, 6 power, 3 copies): attacking with a value pair of Gigs readies up to 2 Merc Legends. Aim for turns with a double @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles|Pepe].
@[Valentino Street Racer] (1 copy): gives another unit with cost 5 or less Adrenaline. Use it on @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles|Pepe] for a first-turn attack that doubles as removal.
@[Les Élémens] (5 cost): bottom-decks the opponent’s lowest-power unit. @[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy|Voodoo Boy] into @[Les Élémens] is the ideal curve.
@[Trust No One] (1 cost): lowers a Gig by up to 3, and you draw a card if you control a min Gig. Pair it with @[Pyramid Song].
@[Pyramid Song] (3 cost): -5 power to a rival unit (printed as -4) or bottom-deck a power-0 unit. You get both effects if your D4 is at min.
@[Nocturne OP55 N1|Nocturne] (3 cost, or 1 if your fixer area is empty): draw 2, or stop a unit from attacking. Play it early so Alt or Lizzy can reuse it.
@[Peace Offering]: never sell the first copy. It sets a Gig to match another Gig, and you draw if that makes a value pair.
@[Take Control] and @[Floor It]: Quick tricks. @[Take Control] makes a rival unit steal 1 fewer Gig, and @[Floor It] gives -1 power and draws a card.
@[Chrome Reverie]: stops a rival unit from attacking, and with a min Gig it Calls a Legend for free.
@[Memory Relapse]: spends a rival unit so it can’t ready. @[Towerfall] is the sweeper (-5 to all rival units).
Alt: replays a Program from your trash. Keep key Programs there, especially @[Les Élémens].
One-of utility cards:
@[Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon|Lizzy Wizzy]: a blocker that replays a cheap Program.
@[Placide: Voodoo Sentinel|Placide]: an 8-cost threat, but don’t slam it just because you hit 8 Eddies.
@[Maman Brigitte: Spirit of Death|Maman Brigitte]: costs you two Programs, so keep it to one copy. It’s better against decks that don’t equip often.
descSections.mulligan:
Keep: @[Jacked-In Voodoo Boy] going first, a @[Trust No One] + @[Pyramid Song] combo, or a 4-cost @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles|Pepe] going second.
Mulligan: multiple @[Nocturne OP55 N1|Nocturnes] with no turn-1 play, or hands built around @[Valentino Street Racer|Street Racer] too early.
You only get one mulligan, so a playable hand beats a risky one.
descSections.sideboard:
For the mirror: @[Sandayu Oda: Hanako's Guardian|Sandayu Oda], extra @[Valentino Street Racer|Street Racers] and @[Psycho Squad].
Against red/red/blue: extra @[Maman Brigitte: Spirit of Death|Maman Brigitte].
@[Modded Kusanagi]: a sideboard card, not main deck.

descSections.notes:
Missing 3 Panam and 1 overwatch
Weak to blue (blue bottom-decks and Jackie does not protect against it). Jackie is a Go Solo Legend and easy to make a 10; you could swap Jackie for Padre. Based on the YouTube transcript linked above.
descSections.overview: Casual, fun green/yellow/red (Dexter, Panam, Jackie) deck built around @[@[Panam Palmer: Nomad Cavalry]]. For 2 Eddies and spending her, you can move a Gear from this Legend to an unequipped friendly unit; if that readies the unit, it can attack even if it's already been attacked. Panam lets you get multiple attacks in. Not competitively viable and has many weaknesses, but it's super fun and wins games at locals.
descSections.early: Going second, play on curve (a four, then a four, then a one, etc.), though this can put you behind on calling Legends - Panam does not care about that. Going first, same plan.
descSections.mid: 3 - 6: play @[Panam Palmer: Nomad Cavalry]  (or call a Legend), attack with her, draw with @[Overwatch: Panam's Gift] . Put gear on Panam first, then move it onto a unit to ready it. @[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles|Pepe] readies two Merc Legends on attack if you control a value pair.
descSections.late: Next turn attack with Panam, play @[Overwatch: Panam's Gift|Overwatch] on another unit, move it over to her and attack again, stealing 2 more (3 Gigs, or steal a Gig and kill something). @[Overwatch: Panam's Gift|Overwatch] draws 6 for a net of 4 cards after discarding 2. Use Panam to fire the gun, not just to move it around.
descSections.combos:
@[Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles|Pepe Najarro]: if he attacks while you control a value pair he readies two Merc Legends, re-using Panam's ability and refunding its cost (2 Eddies becomes a manageable cost). Needs some setup.
@[Overwatch: Panam's Gift|Overwatch]: Panam's Gift: best unit in the deck. Draw so many cards, even one turn can draw six. @[Overwatch: Panam's Gift|Overwatch] on a Legend has only one known answer (Haywood Ripper), because it's too big to hit with @[Detonate]. Put it on Panam so you get value now and later.
@[Mantis Blades], @[Satori: Sword of Saburo|Satori]: the mandatory Gear. @[Satori: Sword of Saburo|Satori] lets you discard a card, then defeat a spent rival unit with cost equal to or less than the discarded card's cost (power doesn't matter). Discard a 5 and you can kill anything with cost 5 or less.
@[Mantis Blades], @[Satori: Sword of Saburo|Satori], @[Sandevistan]: the Gear suite (12 Gear total), the ones I consider mandatory.
@[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo|Meredith]: pretty good with @[Sandayu Oda: Hanako's Guardian|Sandayu Oda] as a restanding effect; play more @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo|Meredith] or more Panam depending on the matchup.
@[Nadia: Fighting Through Grief|Nadia]: in the list as a recovery tool.
@[(Don't Fear) The Reaper]: catch-all removal by itself. Spend all rival units then defeat a spent unit; kills anything for 7 Eddies, spends all their stuff, clears blockers and lets you attack spent things. We have nothing above 7, so Reaper and @[Sandayu Oda: Hanako's Guardian|Sandayu Oda] are the big ones.
@[Sandayu Oda: Hanako's Guardian|Sandayu Oda]: clears most things, also a 7 with pseudo-Adrenaline; he cares about pairs which we make lots of. Not in every green deck, but fits this one.
@[Wild in the Streets]: handles the 5+ cost units that are harder to deal with; Reaper takes care of the problem for big expensive units.
@[Peace Offering], @[Synapse Burnout], @[Industrial Assembly]: standard Programs; @[Industrial Assembly] matters less than @[Peace Offering]. @[Synapse Burnout] is removal for other red/yellow shells.
@[Valentino Street Racer], @[Detonate], @[Riot Shield]: classic tech/low-cost cards. @[Detonate] catches Gear; @[Riot Shield] is good against ghost solo Legends.
descSections.sideboard: Tech from the video: @[Valentino Street Racer|Valentino Street Racers] help against blue decks, @[Detonate] catches Gear, one extra @[Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo|Meredith], @[Nadia: Fighting Through Grief|Nadia] and @[Synapse Burnout] for red/yellow matchups. Build swap plans below (e.g. vs Blue) to see the post-board deck.
